item.title: Windows 11 Updates Add Interactive Search and Xbox Shortcuts
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Digital Trends Original headline: Windows 11 Insider Builds Introduce Enhanced Search Features and Xbox Gaming Shortcuts
Microsoft is updating Windows 11 via Insider Preview builds, adding interactive search features and Xbox gaming shortcuts. Beta Build 26220.9836 and Experimental Build 26340.9843 let users adjust screen brightness, volume, and cursor size via inline sliders in search results. They can manage Bluetooth, WiFi, and power settings without exiting gaming mode. Search now filters results by categories like files, actions, or web results, showing file details and contextual info such as weather, stock prices, and facts. Microsoft Store app suggestions are toggleable through Privacy & security settings. The Verge noted search can trigger actions like making calls or sending texts via connected phones, with Android support already available and iPhone integration expected early 2024. Users can train the search feature by rating results with thumbs-up/down icons. Privacy controls for commercial customers include a new Intune policy restricting Feedback Hub submissions to internal organizations. Updates are available to Insiders through multiple channels, indicating ongoing testing before broader release.

item.title: Android SMS exploit can crash phones remotely via text messages
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Android’s new ‘SMS of Death’ exploit can crash your phone without you doing anything
A security researcher has discovered a critical Android vulnerability dubbed 'SMS of Death' that allows attackers to remotely crash smartphones via malicious text messages. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-58882, exploits how Android processes WAP Push messages, triggering errors in the telephony framework and causing cellular service disruptions, call drops, or reboot loops. Security researcher Mark Blaszczyk notified Google in May and published proof-of-concept code on October 29, demonstrating the attack on Pixel and Samsung devices. Google has released a fix for Android 14 through 17 via October 2026 security updates, but the vulnerability wasn't listed in its security bulletin. Older Android 12 and 13 devices remain unpatched, leaving them vulnerable. The exploit is a denial-of-service attack, not a data theft tool, and no widespread attacks have been confirmed. Users are advised to check for security patches and install updates, though recovery may require technical methods like ADB commands. The flaw does not require user interaction to trigger.

item.title: BetMGM pays MGM $34M as Strip earnings drop 12%
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Original headline: BetMGM cash reaches MGM as Strip earnings fall 12% and US iGaming growth slows
BetMGM paid MGM $34 million in distributions and brand license fees in Q3 2026, while MGM's Las Vegas Strip earnings fell 12%. BetMGM's net revenue rose 7% to $710 million, with iGaming revenue up 6% to $483 million. However, its iGaming growth lagged the US market, which grew 12% year-over-year, the slowest rate on record. BetMGM's nine-month adjusted EBITDA reached $185 million, but it now expects results near the bottom of its revenue and EBITDA guidance. Total payments to owners Entain and MGM totaled $68 million, including $50 million in cash distributions. Regional Operations revenue fell due to a $546 million asset sale, but same-store sales grew slightly. MGM Digital revenue rose to $184 million, with EBITDAR losses narrowing. CEO Bill Hornbuckle noted digital businesses delivered strong revenue growth. The next test for the online market comes from DraftKings, which reports results November 5.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Anthropic Launches Claude Duet Waitlist for Pro Users
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How to use Claude Duet when it rolls out to you
Anthropic released Claude Duet, an AI agent available to Pro and Max subscribers in the US via a waitlist. Users must join the waitlist by providing personal details, phone type, and work description. Duet is included with the $20/month Pro plan, differing from OpenAI's higher-priced options. The agent proactively manages tasks, generates daily briefings, schedules meetings, creates forecasts, and builds web apps. It uses connected accounts and data from the Claude account, with usefulness depending on shared digital life. Anthropic states Duet 'tells you what needs your attention each morning' and 'reaches out when one is done or needs your approval.' Privacy concerns arise as utility hinges on data shared with Anthropic.

item.title: Binance CEO claims 90% of stolen $6.3B has been replenished
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Binance CEO says 90 percent of stolen assets have been ‘replenished’
Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance users in a crypto heist. CEO Changpeng Zhao claims 90 percent of the stolen assets have been replenished, with the remaining 10 percent consisting of less liquid tokens that may take longer to acquire. Binance stated it will fully cover the financial impact of the stolen funds through transparent reporting and concrete actions. Withdrawals remain paused but are scheduled to resume by Sunday, November 1, 2025, as per the company’s previously stated timeline. The firm emphasized its commitment to resolving the incident through measurable progress and user-focused solutions.

item.title: Bolt Graphics powers on first Zeus GPU test chip
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Bolt Graphics powers on its first Zeus GPU
Bolt Graphics has powered on its first Zeus GPU test chip, a 12nm design made by TSMC that ran without issues. The chip measures 6mm² and uses 1.4 watts, compared to 35 watts for its previous FPGA setup. It features dedicated hardware for electromagnetic simulation, aiding radar and camera lens design. CEO Darwesh Singh claimed the chip can run complex physics algorithms in hardware, surpassing internal estimates. The Zeus GPU, built on RISC-V cores, will combine LPDDR5X memory and DDR5 SO-DIMM slots for up to 384GB capacity. Bolt aims to debut the chip on TSMC's N5P process in 2028, avoiding wafer supply competition. The company raised $100 million at a $700 million valuation and targets studios, engineers, and scientists first, with plans to expand into gaming and AI. It claims Zeus could offer 10 times faster path tracing than Nvidia's RTX 5090 and cut compute costs by 17 times. Over 14,000 users signed up for early access, though no customers were named.

item.title: Samsung’s AI Glasses Launch in December, Limited to US and South Korea
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Samsung’s first AI glasses could arrive in December, but only in two countries
Samsung’s AI-powered smart glasses are set for a December launch, limited to the US and South Korea. The release, initially planned for November, has been delayed, with no official confirmation of the exact date or pricing. The glasses use Google’s Android XR platform and Gemini AI for real-time translation, navigation, and voice-activated tasks. They feature a Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 processor and up to nine hours of battery life. Samsung collaborated with eyewear brands Gentle Monster and Warby Parker on four design iterations. The first version lacks a built-in display, relying on camera and voice interactions, with a future model rumored to include a screen. The company aims to gauge customer response before expanding to other regions, though no timeline for global availability or pricing details has been announced.

item.title: USB-IF sets maximum cable lengths for different USB versions
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How long is too long for a USB cable?
USB-IF sets maximum cable lengths for different USB versions. USB 1.0/2.0 cables have a 16.4-foot limit, while USB 3.0-3.2 cables are limited to 9.8 feet. USB 4 cables are restricted to 2.6 feet. Longer cables degrade signal quality due to electrical resistance, causing slower data transfer and reduced power delivery. Manufacturers can produce longer cables, but performance declines beyond USB-IF guidelines. Active USB cables or extenders can mitigate signal loss but are more expensive and require additional power. Powered USB hubs offer another solution, though overloading a hub can reduce performance. Proper cable length ensures optimal USB functionality.

item.title: Modular Keyboard Lets Users Build Custom Layouts with Magnetic Key Modules
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: This 'truly modular' keyboard can be built like a Lego set — meaning you can add as many keys as you like
MIT student Nathan Alspaugh developed Keybytes, an open-source modular keyboard system allowing users to assemble custom layouts using magnetically connected Keybit modules. Each Keybit contains a RISC-V microcontroller for independent key operation, with dimensions matching a standard 1U keyboard unit. The system includes a central Keyword controller with an Arm Cortex-M4 microcontroller, USB-C connectivity, and power management. A full-size configuration using two Keyword controllers and 110 Keybits costs approximately $900, reflecting the cumulative cost of individual components, PCBs, and 3D-printed enclosures. While flexible, the project remains early-stage, with limited module combinations and no completed full-size layout in current documentation. Keybits use Cherry MX switches and magnetic connections for reconfigurable layouts, but lack dedicated lighting. Future features like RGB lighting, rotary controls, and fingerprint sensors are proposed but not confirmed.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: AirPods Disconnecting? Adjust These Settings to Fix It
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Why your AirPods keep disconnecting without warning: These settings can fix it
AirPods disconnecting without warning can often be resolved by adjusting device settings. The issue may stem from automatic switching between multiple Apple devices. Users should change the 'Connect to this iPhone/iPad/Mac' setting to 'When Last Connected to This iPhone/iPad' on all devices to prevent frequent reconnections. On Macs, this is found in Bluetooth settings. Proper earbud fit and clean ear tips are also critical, as loose fit or dirty tips can trigger disconnections. Automatic Ear Detection, which pauses playback when buds are removed, can be disabled in Settings if it causes unintended interruptions. If problems persist, users should forget the device in Bluetooth settings, update firmware by leaving AirPods near a Wi-Fi-connected device for 30 minutes, or perform a reset. Persistent issues may require unpairing and re-pairing the AirPods or a full reset as a last resort.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Four Linux Commands Simplify Complex Terminal Tasks
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: These 4 small Linux commands make complex terminal tasks feel effortless
Four Linux commands simplify complex terminal tasks. xargs processes lists of files by splitting them into batches, enabling efficient batch operations like deleting log files. It handles edge cases like filenames with spaces using null separators and supports parallel processing with -P 4. tee captures pipeline output to files while maintaining real-time display, useful for logging builds or configurations. It bypasses permission issues when using sudo. watch runs commands at intervals to monitor changes, such as tracking disk space or service status, with options to adjust refresh rates and highlight differences. comm compares sorted files line by line, identifying unique or shared entries between lists, and works with process substitution for large datasets. These tools reduce the need for manual loops and temporary files, streamlining workflows for administrators and developers.

item.title: The reason most electrical plug prongs have holes in them
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Electrical plug prongs have holes primarily for manufacturing alignment and safety during production. Manufacturers use the holes to position metal blades before molding and as lockout tags. Historically, the holes interacted with a detent feature in outlets to secure plugs, but modern standards now require outlets to hold plugs without holes. The detent system, once part of NEMA standards, was phased out by UL revisions that prioritized easier plug removal. Most manufacturers continue using holes in plugs for compatibility with older outlets, though they are no longer necessary for electrical function. Plugs without holes are safe and functional, meeting current safety requirements. Users should check receptacle condition, not plug prongs, if connections feel loose. Replacing outdated outlets is recommended over modifying plugs. Holes in prongs are optional but ensure backward compatibility with older receptacles.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Phone screen unresponsiveness troubleshooting steps
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How to fix your phone screen when it's unresponsive to touch​
Phone screen unresponsiveness can often be resolved with troubleshooting steps. Begin by checking for physical damage, removing screen protectors, and cleaning the screen. If the issue persists, restart the device using model-specific force restart methods. For iOS, press volume buttons and the side button; for Android, hold the power button. If software causes the problem, enter safe mode to identify third-party app conflicts. Resetting settings or performing a factory reset may be necessary, though this erases all data. Screen mirroring allows control via a computer if the screen is completely unresponsive, requiring prior setup. For iPhone users, mirroring works with macOS Sequoia or later, while Android users can use Phone Link or Scrcpy. If all else fails, seek professional repair for potential hardware issues.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Microsoft Teams Adds Four Key Features for Enhanced Collaboration
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: 4 important features you should know if you use Microsoft Teams
Microsoft Teams introduced four key features to enhance user experience. A meeting countdown timer, available since mid-2025, allows users to set a timer up to 100 minutes visible to attendees with presenter rights. Voice isolation, using AI to reduce background noise, requires a voice profile setup and can be toggled during calls. Live transcription, launched in 2021, provides real-time transcriptions with speaker differentiation and is available post-meeting. Lastly, unsent message drafts are now accessible in the left panel, added in March 2026, letting users recover incomplete messages. These updates aim to improve meeting efficiency, communication clarity, and task management within the platform.

item.title: Darkbloom Warns of Sharp Drop in AI Token Costs
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Firm that lets you rent out your idle Mac for AI inference workloads warns of plummeting token costs
Darkbloom, a decentralized AI inference network, warns of falling token costs as Anthropic's price per million tokens dropped 77% in five months, to $0.62 in October 2026 from $2.65 in May. Kydo of Eigen Labs notes data centers have become cheaper, with NVIDIA clusters offering 20x more output and margins allowing 90% price cuts. Users running M5 Pro Mac Minis could earn up to $192 monthly, but median earnings are $159.86, translating to $36.77 monthly after the price drop. AI token prices are falling faster than Moore’s Law, with some reports stating 50% annual cost reductions. OpenRouter’s focus on decode speed and quantization disadvantages users without top-tier Apple chips. Darkbloom plans to analyze model demand, expand workloads beyond inference, improve network performance, and seek new clients outside OpenRouter to mitigate earnings declines.

item.title: Developer creates full Intel 486 PC emulator in browser
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Developer builds a complete Intel 486 PC emulator in a browser
Developer Jan de Jager has built a full Intel 486 PC emulator in a browser using pure JavaScript. The Retro486 Modular Browser PC project allows users to boot a live demo with a single click, featuring a CRT monitor interface for DOS commands, games, and applications. Configuration tabs let users adjust motherboard designs, add/remove expansion cards, and customize storage. The emulator includes preloaded OS and software disks, though some games like Doom and Wolfenstein 3D faced errors. A Storage Bay tab lets users manage floppy images and create hard drives. The System & Diagnostics tab enables CPU model changes and memory inspection. Version 0.1 of the project, updated within a week, supports browser persistence and cached ROMs. The emulator, hosted on GitHub, offers a dependency-free experience for retro computing enthusiasts.

item.title: Starbucks Explores Facial Recognition for Customer Recognition
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Facial Recognition Could Be Coming to a Starbucks Near You
Starbucks is exploring facial recognition technology to recognize customers, personalize digital menus, and streamline payments. CEO Brian Niccol stated during an earnings call that the company is "early in this work" and will "test, learn and scale what works." The initiative is part of broader AI investments, including background models for drive-thru order accuracy by 2027. While Starbucks did not explicitly name facial recognition in the call, consumer backlash has already emerged on platforms like X and Bluesky, with critics calling the potential rollout "intrusive and weird business practices." The company has not announced a timeline for deployment, emphasizing ongoing testing before scaling the technology.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Apple AirPods Battery Drain: Causes and Fixes
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Why your Apple AirPods' battery drains so fast and how to make it last longer
Apple AirPods drain quickly due to factors like frequent short use, leaving them out of their case, and active features like ANC and Spatial Audio. Lithium-ion batteries in AirPods degrade after 300-500 charge cycles, reducing listening time. Apple rates AirPods 4 with ANC at four hours with ANC on and five hours off. Leaving earbuds out of the case causes continuous power drain, while dirty contacts or earwax can block charging. Cleaning with a lint-free cloth or isopropyl alcohol (avoiding charging ports) helps. Disabling ANC and Spatial Audio extends battery life. Optimized Battery Charging, enabled via Settings, learns charging habits to prolong battery health. If issues persist, Apple offers free battery service for devices with less than 80% capacity under AppleCare+.

item.title: Nintendo Announces First Pikmin Day Celebrations
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Happy Pikmin Day Eve
Nintendo announced Pikmin Day on November 1st, marking the first annual celebration. During the Pikmin Day Direct, Shigeru Miyamoto revealed details about Pikmin 4 for the Switch 2, including a Dandori Academy mode with limited testing on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. The mobile app Pikmin Bloom will receive Secret Caves, where players battle enemies and explore to win treasure. The Switch 2’s built-in microphone will allow voice commands to control Oatchi, the space dog. Miyamoto also debuted the first episode of the Hello! Pikmin series, with additional episodes planned for December and beyond. The shorts expand on the success of last year’s Close to You animation. The event highlights Nintendo’s ongoing engagement with the Pikmin franchise through new gameplay features and multimedia content.

item.title: France approves internet data tax targeting major tech companies
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: French lawmakers approve $11.2 billion internet tax based on traffic usage, costs $0.06 per gigabyte of content accessed
French lawmakers approved a tax targeting internet data usage, levying €0.055 per gigabyte of content sent to French users. The measure, introduced by socialist lawmaker Laurent Lhardit, aims to generate €10 billion annually by taxing major platforms like Google, Netflix, TikTok, and Meta. The tax, set to be included in France’s 2027 budget, requires internet service providers to track data volumes and report to regulators. Lhardit argued the tax would not shift costs to users, citing free services like TikTok as examples. Opponents, including government ministers, raised privacy concerns over data measurement and monitoring. The proposal faces further parliamentary scrutiny and must clear France’s budget process. Similar digital taxes exist in other European countries, with Meta planning to offset costs through location-based fees. The tax targets companies generating substantial data traffic, excluding advertising revenue or subscriptions. Content delivery networks like Akamai are also included. The measure could affect global tech firms, which account for half of France’s annual data traffic of 200 billion gigabytes.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Why your Spotify might be using so much storage
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Spotify can consume significant phone storage due to downloaded music and cached data. Users can check storage usage via device settings, with iOS directing to Settings > General > iPhone Storage and Android varying by manufacturer. Clearing Spotify's cache through app settings frees up space, while managing downloads via the app's Your Library tab allows removing specific playlists or albums. Removing all downloads via Settings > Data-saving and offline resets offline access. Audio quality settings impact storage: Lossless downloads use more space (e.g., 22GB) compared to Low quality (around 2GB). Other services like Apple Music and Netflix also offer download management. Web and desktop versions don't store offline music. Adjusting media quality settings or clearing cache periodically helps reclaim storage without sacrificing offline listening.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Roku Remote Has 8 Hidden Menus for Advanced Users
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 8 super-useful Roku shortcuts hiding in your remote (plus a bonus tip)
Roku remote users can access hidden menus by pressing specific button sequences. These menus provide advanced diagnostics and settings. For example, pressing Home x5 > Up > Rewind x2 > Fast Forward x2 restarts the device. The Wi-Fi Secret Screen displays detailed network information including signal strength and packet error rates. The Platform Secret Screen shows device metrics like temperature, CPU speed, and remote details. HDMI Secret Screen reveals TV specifications. Channel Info Screen lists installed apps and internal tools. Development Application Installer allows developers to test apps. Secret Screen displays uptime and software details. Secret Screen 2 offers options like changing screenshot formats and ad banners. A bonus tip suggests using Fast Forward and Rewind to navigate long menus efficiently. These shortcuts require deliberate button presses and may vary by Roku model.

item.title: Apple CEO says company avoids shipping AI for AI’s sake
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Apple CEO says the company doesn’t ‘want to ship AI for AI’s sake’
Apple CEO John Ternus told Wired’s Steven Levy that the company avoids shipping AI solely for its own sake. Ternus, who became CEO in September, acknowledged Apple has lagged in AI compared to competitors, citing delays in advancing Siri. However, he expressed confidence in the company’s current approach, stating Apple will use AI in new products but emphasized that the goal is to create tools users love without them noticing AI’s role. When asked if AI could render apps obsolete, Ternus said such automation might simplify tasks but noted product creation remains a deeply human process. He argued that Apple’s focus is on building meaningful experiences rather than chasing AI trends, stressing that successful integration should feel seamless to users.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Apple AirPods may fail to connect to iPhone due to battery, software, or Bluetooth issues
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Why your Apple AirPods won't connect to your iPhone and how can you fix it
Apple AirPods may fail to connect to iPhone due to battery, software, or Bluetooth issues. Common causes include drained battery, dirt on charging contacts, automatic switching errors, outdated firmware, or Bluetooth being disabled. To resolve, check battery levels by charging, clean contacts, ensure Bluetooth is enabled, and verify software updates via Settings > General > Software Update. If firmware is outdated, charge AirPods for 30 minutes to trigger an update. Resetting AirPods by placing them in the case and entering pairing mode can also fix connections. If issues persist, contact Apple Support for hardware replacement, which may be free under warranty or AppleCare+.

item.title: Samsung Discontinues News App, No Replacement Announced
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: The Samsung News app is being discontinued, and there's no replacement yet
Samsung is discontinuing the News app, effective December 21, 2026. The shutdown will remove the app, its home screen widget, and the media page accessible via swiping right. Users in India and South Korea are being notified to remove the widget before the service ends. All user data, including personalization settings and account profiles, will be deleted post-shutdown, with some information temporarily retained due to legal requirements. Samsung News replaced Samsung Free in 2023 and succeeded Samsung Daily, which was replaced by Bixby Home in 2019. No direct replacement is announced, though Google Discover is a potential alternative already available on Galaxy devices. Samsung has not specified if other regions will follow the same schedule, but the native news experience is set to end.

item.title: Gen Z Rewrites CVs to Avoid AI Detection, Others Face Similar Challenges
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Neither side thinks hiring is working': Gen Z job seekers are rewriting their CVs as they're worried about sounding like AI — and they aren't alone
Gen Z job seekers are rewriting CVs to avoid appearing AI-generated, as AI screening dominates hiring processes. A Greenhouse survey of 1,100 UK and Ireland applicants found 81% are rejected without human contact. 97% wish they could showcase non-application skills, highlighting resume homogenization. 42% experienced AI interviews in the past year, with 57% finding them helpful for skill demonstration. Sharawn Tipton, Greenhouse’s Chief People Officer, stated neither candidates nor employers believe hiring is working. Employers face challenges distinguishing applicants with AI-polished resumes. Tipton called for a system that provides fair opportunities, criticizing current AI screening as harmful. Ophir Samson suggested building trust in hiring processes from the start, emphasizing transparency for applicants.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: WhatsApp Adds Group Status, Permanent Pins, and Message Filters
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: WhatsApp group chats get permanent message pins, private Status updates, and more
WhatsApp is rolling out four new features to enhance group chat management. Group Status allows users to share updates exclusively within a specific group, visible only to members and disappearing after 24 hours. Permanent message pinning now lets users keep messages at the top of conversations indefinitely, addressing the need for long-term accessibility. A dedicated filter for mentions and replies consolidates unread messages directed at the user, streamlining task management. The app also enables sharing recent message history with new group members even after they join, maintaining end-to-end encryption. These updates aim to tackle issues with information overload in busy groups, improving visibility and organization. WhatsApp previously introduced message history sharing when adding members and is testing additional features like search shortcuts and scheduled messages for future updates.

item.title: SALES: 5 Open-Source Apps Every Windows User Should Try
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 5 essential open-source apps every Windows user should install
Blender, a free 3D modeling suite, competes with premium software like 3ds Max and Maya, offering all-in-one tools for animation, sculpting, and rendering. Its latest versions include HDR support and experimental physics features. OBS Studio remains the top choice for live streaming, supporting hardware encoders and multi-track audio, with a thriving plugin ecosystem. VLC, a long-standing open-source video player, handles nearly any media format and is pre-installed on many Windows systems. LocalSend, a file-sharing app, enables encrypted transfers between devices over local networks without internet, handling large files at high speeds. ShareX, a screenshot tool, offers advanced editing, scrolling capture, and workflows for screen recording and OCR. These apps exemplify the strength of the open-source Windows ecosystem, rivaling closed-source alternatives in functionality and reliability.

item.title: Snowflake Emphasizes Choosing Right AI Models for Business Efficiency
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: 'The reality is that not every task requires the most advanced or expensive model available': Snowflake explains why finding the right AI model can make all the difference in helping your business succeed
Snowflake emphasizes selecting the right AI model for business efficiency, shifting from prioritizing model power to task-specific optimization. Grace Adamson, AI Product Marketing Manager at Snowflake, explains that not every task requires the most advanced or expensive model. Dynamic model routing automatically matches workloads to models balancing quality, speed, and cost, reducing AI spend while maintaining performance. This approach, called intelligence efficiency, allows organizations to use efficient models for repetitive tasks and frontier models for complex reasoning. Snowflake’s platform enables governance, cost tracking, and seamless model selection, addressing challenges like model overload and unpredictable AI spend. Observability tools track usage, latency, and costs, helping businesses measure ROI through metrics like productivity gains and revenue impact. The company advocates for flexible, model-agnostic strategies, ensuring organizations maximize AI value without overpaying for unnecessary capabilities.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: INSTRUCTION: 3D Printer Repurposes Old Phones, Tablets, and Smartwatches
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Here's how I use a 3D printer to give my old phones, smartwatches, and smart home gear a second life
A 3D printer is used to repurpose old phones, tablets, and smartwatches. For a 2009 Chevy Silverado lacking Android Auto, an old Amazon Fire Tablet is mounted with a custom bracket made from a discarded display mount. A Unihertz Titan 2 Elite phone is transformed into a gaming handheld with a 3D-printed Game Boy-style cover, featuring tactile buttons and RetroArch compatibility. A Pixel Watch is modified with a scroll wheel and buttons to function as a less watch-like device. A Google Home Mini is paired with a phone via Bluetooth automation to serve as a smart display, replacing the limited Nest Hub experience. The projects highlight reusing existing hardware through custom 3D-printed accessories.
